recovery.sweep_evm/send_evm_amount silently skip gas-funding when treasury_pk not provided by returning a soft error — good, but caller (direct_deposit_worker) MUST always pass treasury_pk; verify that path in an integration test.
_TOKEN_GAS_LIMIT_BY_CHAIN for arbitrum=1_500_000 is very high (L2 accounting) — reasonable, but on Arbitrum gas price is tiny so top-up remains small; still worth documenting the reason inline.
_gas_price uses max(network, floor). If BSC network price ever spikes and floor is smaller, we correctly use network price. Good.
send_evm_amount only funds gas if treasury_pk != privkey; correct guard against self-funding loops.
No retry/backoff on _fund_gas wait_for_transaction_receipt(timeout=180). On BSC congestion this could hang the request thread; consider moving to a background sweeper.

Consider adding an integration test that mocks web3 to simulate a full ERC-20 sweep and asserts gas topup value == _token_gas_limit(chain) * _gas_price * 1.1 exactly (unit-level check of the funded amount).

rca of the issue: Original complaint: gas top-up sent to newly-generated deposit addresses was wastefully large. RCA: recovery.py used a 1 gwei floor for gas price and a fixed 100_000 gas limit with 1.3x buffer, producing ~1.3e-4 BNB top-up per sweep on BSC (many times more than needed). Fix: (1) Dropped BSC floor to protocol minimum 0.1 gwei (100_000_000 wei). (2) Replaced fixed 100_000 gas limit + 1.3x with tight per-chain _TOKEN_GAS_LIMIT_BY_CHAIN (bsc 60000) and 1.1x _GAS_FUND_BUFFER. (3) Removed estimate_gas calls entirely (they would fail on gas-less deposit addresses anyway). Result: BSC top-up is now ~6.6e-6 BNB — a ~20x reduction. Verified by direct module inspection + endpoint tests.
